definition: Subjugation means the bringing of a people under complete and lasting control by force.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word subjugation. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know subjugation should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Chroniclers date the delta's subjugation not from the last battle but from the first census: the year every household was counted, taxed, and forbidden to travel without the conqueror's pass.

Enslavement goes further than subjugation — past the complete control of a people to outright ownership of the persons in it.

Domination is control from above in any arena — a firm can dominate a market, a team its league — and it needs no conqueror at all. Subjugation is domination's harshest political case: a people brought under a victor's complete and lasting control, with force standing behind every rule.

Oppression names the weight itself — unjust laws, crushing burdens — and rulers can oppress their own citizens without conquering anyone. Subjugation names the bringing-under and the holding-under; a subjugated people can even be governed with a light touch, and the control is no less total.

When the khan's army took the river cities, the fighting lasted a single summer; the subjugation took a generation.
First the walls came down, then the old royal courts; judges the khan appointed heard every dispute, and his tax collectors kept the ledgers.
A grandmother in Osk could remember voting for her guild's council.
Her grandchildren could not imagine it: every office in the city now answered, link by link, to the khan's tent.
Chroniclers note that the khan's rule was not especially cruel — grain was cheap, the roads were safe — and that this changed nothing about what it was.
The river cities kept their language and their festivals.
What they no longer kept was any thread of rule that began at home.
